label: text
text: Several motor accidents occurred during the week-end, none fatal, but a European resident was rather seriously injured while cycling yesterday and now lies in hospital.

label: text

label: text

label: text

label: text
text: A Dangerous Bend?

label: text
text:
Mr. de Veer was on the round-the-island road, going from Stanley towards Shaukiwan. He was on an Indian solo. Taking a bend at an incline, he seemed either to lose control or to have rounded at a faulty angle, with the result that he charged into the embankment.
He was thrown off by a violent compact and his left leg was seriously injured above the ankle.
Dr. J. K. Milward, a local practitioner, happened to be passing. First aid was rendered by the doctor, who also took Mr. de Veer to hospital.

label: text
text: Mr. de Veer is a sub-accountant in the local office of the Netherlands Trading Society.

label: text
text: A friend of his, who was cycling with him, on another machine, notified the police.

label: text
text: Several of the passengers received cuts, none serious.

label: text
text: Community of Views.

label: text
text: Rugby, October 3.

label: text
text: (Sir Austen Chamberlain on his way home from Italy had an interview in Paris with M. Briand, the French Foreign Minister.

label: text
text: was issued to the Press stating that in the course of an interview, "M. Briand and Sir Austen Chamberlain emphasised and defined the community of views and purposes for the solution of international problems at the present issue. Sir Austen Chamberlain who, at Geneva, had been informed of the intention of his French colleague to hold conversations with the German Foreign Minister, had to leave Switzerland before the interview at Thoiry and has been resting during a fortnight's cruise in the Mediterranean. Before returning to London and resuming work at the Foreign Office he desired to stop in Paris to meet the French Foreign Minister. The two statesmen have examined the foreign situation and in particular the question of Franco-German relations, the direction of which has been defined by the Locarno agreement and the Thoiry conversations. The conversations took place in a favourable atmosphere, which was assured by the personal relations between the two Ministers. They have been able to emphasise that their entire interests of peace remains closer, more cordial, and more secure than ever.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain will back in London this evening.—British Wireless Service.

label: text

label: text
text: SUN UNDECIDED, NOT UNREADY.

label: text
text: [From Our Special Correspondent]

label: text
text: Such are the vagaries of war! While capturing some of his enemy and prosecuting an offensive against the heart of the Cantonese Merchel Sun Chuan

label: text
text: fang is still lending ear to peace overtures.

label: text
text: As gossip in Shanghai said when he won his first victory, he is not Sun the Unready, but Sun the Undecided.

label: text
text: Still preaching "Pao Ching, An Min" (peace if you leave me alone), he continues to hammer away at the northern flank of the Cantonese line.

label: text
text: East weck, his strategic moves between the lower Yangtse and Tayeh Lake have fully bent back the salient which the southerners had put into Kiangsi.

label: text
text: Now there seems to be a full in the victorious march towards Wuchang (in Hupeh) and the only reason is because Sun Chuan still hopes for peace.

label: text
text: This attitude is hard to explain. When Chang Kai-shek wheeled to the right, he unconsciously followed the example of a famous Cantonese rebel '70 years ago, who kept on the southern bank of the Yangtse and trekked to Nanking. That rising, by the way was quelled by General Gordon (of Khartoum).

label: text
text: Is Sun Chuan-fang to prove the Gordon of to-day, from the point of view of the North

label: text
text: He has three main armies, fighting towards the west, from Kiangsi. The most southerly is making little or no progress: The "centre" has more than held its ground and is forcing back the Cantonese. The northern wing has won all the honours.

label: text
text: But there now seems to be hesitation, giving the appearance that Sun Chuan-fang would still welcome peace, rather than war, provided he got some material benefit.
